messages.subject: Uncertainty estimation in DSM in R. Variance propagation
parts:
Hi, I am trying to estimate uncertainty with DSM in R and try to run the following sentences, which feed the dsm.var.prop function.


preddata.varprop <- split(preddata, 1:nrow(preddata))
offset.varprop <- as.list(rep(off.set, nrow(preddata)))
mod1.varprop <- dsm.var.prop(mod1, pred.data = preddata.varprop, off.set = offset.varprop)

These sentences come from the self explanatory mexico example...

I get an Error message when calling dsm.var,prop:


Error in UseMethod("predict") :   no applicable method for 'predict' applied to an object of class "NULL"

I googled for help in R but no help. It seems to have something to do with the predict module but the module is running Ok when I predict from the dsm model and the prediction grid... any help?

messages.author: 512996ea4ff0ea65
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Uncertainty estimation in DSM in R. Variance propagation
parts:
After updating the packages and seeing that nothing changed, I{ve sent the script and data to David Miller, who answered what I copy below.

The point is that I was trying to estimate variance with a code aiming to evaluate uncertainty in detection function. As our data comes from strip transects there is no uncertainty in df so the use of this code is wrong.

I copy the answer of David Miller. many thanks and hope it is useful to somebody else...!

And a small advertising:  Using dsm with R is really flexible (at least has many more options in relation of what you can find today in the DISTANCE interface). I know that R may looks criptic but when you pass the learning curve... it gives you more flexibility... so go fot it!



------------------------------------------------------------------------

Hi Adrian,

It looks like the issue is that you're using dsm.var.prop when you don't have a detection function specified -- in your dsm call you use ddf.obj=NULL. dsm.var.prop() is used for variance propagation to ensure that uncertainty from the detection function is propagated into the final model variance. When there is no detection function one should use dsm.var.gam:

mod1.var <- dsm.var.gam(mod1, pred.data = preddata.varprop,off.set = offset.varprop)

then calling summary on the resulting object yields:

> summary(mod1.var)


Summary of uncertainty in a density surface model calculated
 analytically for GAM, with delta method

Approximate asymptotic confidence interval:
      5%     Mean      95%
11271.54 14200.82 17891.36
(Using delta method)

Point estimate                 : 14200.82
Standard error                 : 1679.63
CV of detection function       :
CV from GAM                    :
Total coefficient of variation : 0.1183


I've added some code to dsm to warn folks when trying to do what you did (which I should have done before!), so you can be happy that you've helped someone else in the future.

I am happy to post a summary of this issue to the list, unless you would prefer to send it?

cheers,
--dave

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Uncertainty estimation in DSM in R. Variance propagation
parts:
Adrian, list,

As I recall from the data/code you sent me previously, you didn't
include a detection function in the analysis (effectively strip
transects). The plotting function was expecting a detection function to
tell it about the group size of the observations so they can be plotted.
I have modified dsm so this error doesn't occur again and this will be
in the next CRAN release of dsm.

In the mean time you can either use the latest dsm release from github
via the following mechanism:

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_github("DistanceDevelopment/dsm")

or use observation=FALSE in your call to plot, which will ignore that
part of the code:

plot(mod1.var, xlab = "Easting", ylab = "Northing",observation=FALSE)


Hope this helps!

best,
--dave
